binders: A type Omega equipped with a measurable-space structure.
A measure mu on Omega equipped with the assumption that mu is a probability measure.
Two real-valued functions X, Y : Omega -> Real.
An extended nonnegative real exponent p in [0,infinity].
hypotheses: X belongs to MemLp at exponent p with respect to mu.
Y belongs to MemLp at exponent p with respect to mu.
conclusions: The extended Lp seminorm satisfies norm(X+Y,Lp(mu)) <= norm(X,Lp(mu)) + norm(Y,Lp(mu)), where X+Y is pointwise addition.
mathematical_definitions: ENNReal is the extended nonnegative real line [0,infinity].
MemLp f p mu asserts almost-everywhere strong measurability and finiteness of eLpNorm f p mu.
eLpNorm f p mu is 0 at p=0, the essential-supremum norm at p=infinity, and the usual integral-based Lp seminorm otherwise.
translation.proposition_plain_english: On a probability space, for every extended exponent p at least 1 and every pair of real-valued functions X and Y in Lp, the Lp seminorm of their pointwise sum is at most the sum of their individual Lp seminorms.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The statement is restricted to real-valued functions.
p may equal infinity, so the conclusion includes the essential-supremum case.
The probability-measure assumption is stronger than needed for Minkowski.
If no probability instance exists for mu, the statement is inapplicable to that mu.
MemLp imposes AE strong measurability and finite eLpNorm, so this is not the most general extended-valued inequality.
Because 1<=p, the p=0 branch cannot occur.
ambiguities: The target uses an extended-valued seminorm on raw functions rather than explicit AE quotient classes.
The packet gives only the type, not defining field, of IsProbabilityMeasure; mass-one semantics is inferred from its name.
